items.prompt: Input [3,5,6,1] leaves tails [1,5,6]. What is safe to conclude?

options.text: The array [1,5,6] is necessarily a witness in input order.
options.why: The 1 arrived after 5 and 6, so those three values are not that ordered input subsequence.

options.text: LIS length is 3, but this tails array is not itself a witness.
options.why: Different frontier entries can summarize subsequences from different earlier prefixes.

options.text: LIS length must be 1 because 1 arrived last.
options.why: Earlier increasing subsequences remain valid after later arrivals.

options.text: Replacing the first tail destroys the earlier [3,5,6] subsequence.
options.why: The original observations still exist; frontier replacement does not erase them.

items.explanation: Different frontier entries can summarize subsequences from different earlier prefixes.
